title: De quibusdam eximiis proprietatibus circa divisores potestatum occurrentibus

deep.reconstruction:
This page (pp. 260–261 of the print) continues E557's case-by-case statements of what is in effect Euler's criterion combined with quadratic reciprocity. Let q = 2p+1 be a prime with gcd(a,q) = 1. Fermat gives q | a^{2p} − 1 = (a^p − 1)(a^p + 1), so q divides exactly one of the two factors. Which one depends on whether a is a quadratic residue mod q (Euler's criterion a^p ≡ (a/q) mod q). Euler states this himself in the Problema of §36 on the next page.

The tables give, for each a, the classes of q mod 4a for which q | a^p − 1 (i.e. (a/q) = +1):
- a = 3: q ≡ ±1 mod 12 gives a^p − 1; q ≡ ±5 mod 12 gives a^p + 1.
- a = 5: q ≡ ±1, ±9 mod 20 gives −1; q ≡ ±3, ±7 gives +1.
- a = 6: q ≡ ±1, ±5 mod 24 gives −1; q ≡ ±7, ±11 gives +1.
- a = 7: q ≡ ±1, ±3, ±9 mod 28 gives −1; q ≡ ±5, ±11, ±13 gives +1.
- a = 8: q ≡ ±1, ±7, ±9, ±15 mod 32 gives −1; the remaining odd classes give +1. This is just the law for 2, since 8 = 2·2².
- a = 10 (table on p. 262): q ≡ ±1, ±3, ±9, ±13 mod 40 gives −1; q ≡ ±7, ±11, ±17, ±19 gives +1.

The tables serve the 'Theorema generale' of §32: whether q | a^p − 1 or a^p + 1 depends only on q modulo 4a, and is the same for q and −q mod 4a. This is Euler's (1744/1751/1783) form of the quadratic reciprocity law, stated empirically ('firma demonstratione etiamnum indiget' for the case a = 2 in §25).
errors: No mathematical errors. Every table entry checks against the Legendre-symbol values: (3/q) for q mod 12; (5/q), which depends on q mod 5; (6/q) = (2/q)(3/q); (7/q) for q mod 28; (8/q) = (2/q); and (10/q) = (2/q)(5/q).

Gap (acknowledged in the paper): the dependence on q mod 4a is induced from numerical cases, not proved here. Euler proves only the step from residue to the divisibility of a^p − 1 (Euler's criterion), in §36 ff.

Minor redundancy: for a = 8 the modulus 32 is unnecessary, since mod 8 suffices. Euler's uniform use of 4a hides that the true period is 4·(squarefree part of a), or that part itself when it is ≡ 1 mod 4.

ideas.what: For prime q = 2p+1, q | a^p − 1 iff a is a quadratic residue mod q, otherwise q | a^p + 1.
ideas.where_published: E262 'Theoremata circa residua ex divisione potestatum relicta' and E449 'Disquisitio accuratior circa residua...'; also §36 of this paper

ideas.what: Tables of the residue character of a = 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 by prime class mod 4a, invariant under q → −q.
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic reciprocity (Euler's formulation via classes mod 4a)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Euler; also Legendre (1785/1798); first proved by Gauss (1796, Disquisitiones 1801)
ideas.where_published: E164 (Theoremata circa divisores numerorum in hac forma paa±qbb contentorum), E552 (Observationes circa divisionem quadratorum per numeros primos, Opuscula analytica 1783), and this paper E557

ideas.what: Case a = 8 (equivalently a = 2): character determined by q mod 8.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Fermat/Euler; proved by Lagrange (1775) and Euler
ideas.where_published: E552, E557 §25, and Euler's earlier correspondence/papers

deep.surprise_reason: These are correct, well-known instances of Euler's empirical quadratic reciprocity. Euler's formulation in E552/E557 is thoroughly documented in the historical literature (e.g. Weil, Lemmermeyer's 'Reciprocity Laws'). Nothing here is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The image spans two printed pages (260 and 261). The transcription's split, with Theorema 5 continuing onto p. 261 at 'siue formula 7^p+1', is correct.
For a = 3 and a = 5 the print uses '∓' (e.g. '12n ∓ 5', '20.n ∓ 1'); for later tables it uses '±'. The meaning is identical, and the transcription matches the image.
